back: Profit in absolute terms? Profit relative to capital (ratios, margins)? High enough vs what? Solvency (medium/long term)? Liquidity (short term)?
GAAP (defined by IFRS): revenue, net income, EPS, segment information, discontinued operations. Non-GAAP: EBITDA, operating/recurring profit (until IFRS 18), ROCE, FCF, EVA, net debt.

Net sales − cost of sales = gross margin ± other operating items = EBITDA − D&A, impairment = operating profit ± non-recurring = EBIT − net interest = EBT − tax = NI continuing ± discontinued = net income.

Operating profit + depreciation & amortisation. Non-GAAP, not standardised. Neutralises financing, tax and depreciation policies; ≈ cash from operations before working capital and taxes. Used in valuation and covenants (net debt/EBITDA).
EBITDA after leases (≈ EBITDA − lease payments), used e.g. by telecoms/airlines since IFRS 16 moved rent below EBITDA.
NOPAT / capital employed, NOPAT = EBIT × (1 − t). Capital employed = net non-current assets + working capital needs = equity + net financial debt.
Inventories + trade receivables − trade payables (operating items only, no cash or financial debt).
ROCE = NOPAT margin (NOPAT/sales) × capital employed turnover (sales/capital employed).
ROE = net income / equity (shareholders). ROA = EBIT / total assets. ROI = EBIT / investment (profit centres).
EVA = NOPAT − WACC × capital employed = (ROCE − WACC) × capital employed. Positive → value created. Improve: higher NOPAT, lower capital, lower WACC.

front: Free cash flow to the firm
back: CFO − net capex (or EBIT(1 − t) + D&A − capex − ΔWCN). Cash available to all capital providers; not reduced by dividends or debt repayments.
FCFF + net increase in financial debt − interest × (1 − t) (or NI + D&A − capex − ΔWCN + net borrowing). Reduced by debt repayments.

Management-defined performance measures = non-IFRS subtotals of income/expenses used in public communication. Required: reconciliation, explanation, statement that they are management's view. FCF, ROE, net debt are not MPMs.
